issue: Fine. h₂wĺ̥h₁neh₂i is loc. 'on wool'.

m̥dʰéws is GEN/ABL.SG of médʰu; 'drink mead' wants the object ACC médʰu. A partitive genitive is possible IE syntax, but the English has a plain object, so the case is wrong. Also mudént is AOR 3pl ('became joyful') under present 'rejoice' (gnomic aorist for an aorist-only verb is tolerable; minor).
Fine.
Tier 1 title in old notation; fine.
Final 'He receives the dead' uses h₁áyto (MID AOR 3sg 'took/received'): tense differs from the English present. h₁ésyo démi for 'his (own) house' would better be swéy/swósyo.
Fine; gnomic aorists péh₃t/mérst in the 'whoever drinks' clause are acceptable.
Tier 1 Schleicher-style line; fine.
téh₂ (n. pl. 'them', the téḱneh₂) is followed by masc. népotn̥s 'my grandsons': mixed gender in apposition; tóns would agree with népotn̥s.

'On the other side' is h₂én (gloss 'there, yonder, on the other side'): ok. ǵnéh₃t (aorist 'knew/met') under present 'meets', pért aorist under 'crosses': gnomic past tense in a timeless description; minor tense mismatch.
Fine. tewtéh₂ gloss includes 'heap, pile'.
ǵʰwént (AOR 3pl 'poured') under habitual present 'the women pour milk'; the rest of the text is present.
h₁yód h₁eǵóh₂ séneh₂ h₁ésesi: h₁ésesi is SBJV 2SG, but the subject is h₁eǵóh₂ 'I' ('when I am old'); needs 1SG h₁ésoh₂.
Tier 1 title; fine.
wéy h₁idʰé ménetes: ménetes is PRS 2DU/3DU, but the subject is wéy 'we' ('we remain here'); needs 1PL ménomes.
Genealogy: 'No son was born to Wolf-Fame; his grandson ruled after him' — a grandson without a son needs a daughter's line stated; as written it is odd. Grammar fine.
Fine (ph₂stés 3DU, tóybʰos ABL with fear).
somHóh₁ h₁stā́m 'the two were together/as one' rendered 'were alone': stretched sense.
Fine.
h₁áyto (AOR 'took') and ḱéHst (AOR 'taught') under present English 'takes', 'teaches'; h₁ésyo mogʰéwey 'his boy' would be swéy for 'his own'.
Fine.
Fine; tékst 'wove' (teks- weave, plait).
deywṓs tósmey h₁uséwōm dh₃ih₁ént: h₁uséwōm is GEN.PL of h₁wésus; 'may the gods give him good things' needs the object in the accusative (n. pl. h₁wésu, Od. 24.402 formula per brief). Case error.
Fine; kʷékʷlom gloss includes 'chariot'.
Fine.
kʷís moy wódr̥ ǵʰéwete: ǵʰéwete is 2PL (PRS/IMP/SBJV), but the subject is kʷís 'who' (3SG, 'who will pour'); needs 3SG subjunctive.
Fine.
Fine; plural ǵn̥h₁yónto for a dual subject is the engine's expected fallback (no 3du middle); usmé for 'you two' likewise.
gʷʰénm̥ is PST 1SG 'I was slaying' for 'I have slain' (aorist expected); the quotation is not marked as speech in the PIE, so 'cried his own son slain' reads ambiguously.
